finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: POST /hooks/test passes attacker-supplied req.body.callback directly to axios.post with no scheme, host, IP, or redirect validation, and returns the response status to the caller.
finding.source: req.body.callback (routes.js:20), on the unauthenticated pub router (routes.js:4, :19)

trace.note: pub router is created with no auth middleware
req.body.callback used as axios.post URL with no validation
r.status returned to attacker, giving a status-code oracle

finding.guards_checked: None on the path. No auth middleware on pub router. No URL scheme, host, or private-IP allowlist. No maxRedirects or beforeRedirect control; axios follows redirects by default. Route mounting and body parser are not visible in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:4 creates `pub` with no middleware, and `requireAdmin` (routes.js:7-12) is attached only to `admin` via `admin.use` (routes.js:12). Nothing on the path validates `req.body.callback` before `axios.post` at routes.js:20. Repo-wide grep finds no maxRedirects, beforeRedirect, or URL allowlist.
verdict.reason: At routes.js:19-20, `pub.post("/hooks/test")` passes `req.body.callback` straight to `axios.post` with no scheme, host, or IP check, and `pub` has no auth middleware (routes.js:4), so an unauthenticated caller controls the SSRF target; routes.js:21 returns `r.status` as a status oracle. Caveat: the mount point and body parser are not in the repo, so if the app mounts `pub` behind an auth layer elsewhere, the unauthenticated premise would fail, but nothing visible here shows that.

finding.claim: SSRF via admin diagnostics: GET /diagnostics/fetch passes req.query.url directly to axios.get with no destination validation. Access is limited to admin-role sessions, so the impact is an admin reaching internal hosts.
finding.source: req.query.url (routes.js:15), behind admin.use(requireAdmin) (routes.js:12) and the session role check (routes.js:8)

trace.note: requireAdmin applied to all admin routes
req.query.url passed to axios.get with no validation; redirects followed

finding.guards_checked: Admin role gate (routes.js:8, :12) is enforced. No URL scheme, host, or private-IP validation. Redirects are followed. A url given as an array would cause an error (minor). Whether admins are meant to reach internal networks is not visible in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none closing. The admin gate at routes.js:7-8 (req.session.role !== "admin" returns 403) and routes.js:12 (admin.use(requireAdmin)) limit reachability, but they are not a URL validation guard. No scheme, host, or private-IP check exists before axios.get at routes.js:15.
verdict.reason: All trace lines (routes.js:8, 12, 14, 15, 16) exist and match the claim, but the source req.query.url at routes.js:15 is reachable only by a session with role "admin" (routes.js:8, 12), which is not the unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker the criteria require, so this is an admin-only hardening concern rather than a finding.
